milestone: Edward Jenner developed the smallpox vaccine using cowpox pus, leading to its eventual global eradication in 1980.
Louis Pasteur successfully administered the first rabies vaccine to a human patient bitten by a rabid dog.

transmission_mode: Plant contact / Contaminated soil or tools
milestone: Martinus Beijerinck demonstrated that the infectious agent causing tobacco mosaic disease was a contagious liquid filtrate—coining the modern concept of a virus.
Walter Reed and his team proved that yellow fever is transmitted by mosquitoes, marking the first human virus discovered.
Confirmed to be transmitted by mosquitoes, paving the way for arbovirology.
Karl Landsteiner and Erwin Popper identified poliovirus as the causative agent of poliomyelitis.
Peyton Rous discovered the first tumor-causing virus in chickens, later earning a Nobel Prize.
Caused the catastrophic 'Spanish Flu' pandemic, resulting in tens of millions of deaths worldwide.
W. Smith, C.H. Andrewes, and P. Laidlaw successfully isolated the first human influenza virus.
First isolated from a woman in the West Nile district of Uganda.
Isolated from mosquitoes in Uganda, serving as the prototype for the massive Bunyaviridae family.
Discovered in adenoid tissue cultures by Wallace Rowe and colleagues.
Thomas Peebles and John Enders isolated the live measles virus from a student named David Edmonston.
Sparked the 'Asian Flu' pandemic originating in East Asia.
Isolated independently by Paul Parkman and Thomas Weller, leading to congenital rubella syndrome insights.
Anthony Epstein, Yvonne Barr, and Bert Achong discovered the first human tumor virus linked to Burkitt lymphoma.
Baruch Blumberg discovered the 'Australia antigen,' leading to the identification and blood tests for Hepatitis B.
First recognized during outbreaks among laboratory workers in Marburg and Frankfurt, Germany, exposed to African green monkeys.
Caused the 'Hong Kong Flu' pandemic.
Identified after an outbreak among missionary nurses in Lassa, Nigeria.
Isolated from the urine of a kidney transplant patient, designated by his initials B.K.

transmission_mode: Fecal-oral / Contaminated food and water / Surface contact
milestone: Visualized via immune electron microscopy following an acute gastroenteritis outbreak in Norwalk, Ohio.
Discovered via electron microscopy in duodenal biopsies of children with severe diarrhea.
Discovered accidentally by Yvonne Cossart while screening blood bank donors for Hepatitis B.

transmission_mode: Direct contact (Infected bodily fluids, blood, or tissue)
milestone: Identified near the Ebola River in Zaire (now DRC) during simultaneous severe hemorrhagic fever outbreaks.
Isolated by Ho-Wang Lee from striped field mice, explaining Korean hemorrhagic fever.
Discovered by Bernard Poiesz and Robert Gallo as the first human retrovirus linked to adult T-cell leukemia.
Isolated by Luc Montagnier's team at the Pasteur Institute (and later Robert Gallo) as the cause of AIDS.
Cloned and identified by Michael Choo, Harvey Alter, and Charles Rice after being historically known as 'non-A, non-B hepatitis'.
Identified through immune electron microscopy during a waterborne hepatitis outbreak in India.
Isolated following a mysterious outbreak of severe respiratory illness (HCPS) in the Four Corners region of the USA.
Discovered after an outbreak of severe respiratory disease in horses and humans in Hendra, Brisbane, Australia.
Identified in South America, later proving to be the only hantavirus capable of human-to-human transmission.

transmission_mode: Zoonotic (Direct contact with infected birds or contaminated environments)
milestone: First documented severe human infections from H5N1 avian influenza during an outbreak in Hong Kong.

transmission_mode: Zoonotic (Pig-to-human contact / Contaminated date palm sap)
milestone: Emerging zoonotic virus identified during an outbreak of encephalitis and respiratory illness among pig farmers in Malaysia.
Sudden emergence in New York City, marking the virus's first introduction to the Western Hemisphere.
Emerged in Guangdong, China, sparking a global Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome outbreak.
A novel swine-origin reassortant influenza virus triggered the first 21st-century global flu pandemic.
Identified in Saudi Arabia, causing severe respiratory illness with camels acting as the primary animal reservoir.
Emerged in China, causing significant human cases associated with exposure to live poultry markets.
Triggered a major public health emergency across Latin America due to its association with microcephaly in newborns.
The second-largest Ebola outbreak in history began in the conflict-affected eastern region of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
Emergence of the novel coronavirus in Wuhan, China, leading to the global COVID-19 pandemic.
Accelerated viral evolution tracking through global genomic surveillance yielded key variants of concern.
Discovered in late 2021, driving massive global waves of infection due to high immune evasion and transmission.
Unprecedented multi-country outbreak of mpox spread primarily via sexual networks outside of endemic African regions.

transmission_mode: Zoonotic (Animal contact / Ingestion of unpasteurized infected dairy)
milestone: Massive global epizootic expanded rapidly into marine mammals, wild birds, and commercial dairy cattle herds.
Spread beyond traditional Amazonian basins, causing widespread outbreaks and rare vertical transmission cases in the Americas.

transmission_mode: Direct physical touch / Household and sexual contact
milestone: Intensified international public health focus on clade I mpox strains spreading across Central and East Africa and travelers abroad.
Global health networks fully integrated real-time AI genomic tracking to monitor animal-to-human spillover hot spots.
